title: The Limits of Legal Reasoning
text:
Legal reasoning often turns on the distinction between the letter of a statute and the purpose that animates it. Textualists contend that judges must confine themselves to the ordinary meaning of the words enacted by the legislature, lest they usurp a function that belongs to democratically accountable bodies. Purposivists, by contrast, maintain that a rigid adherence to phraseology can frustrate the very objectives the statute was designed to achieve. The resulting tension is seldom resolved in the abstract, and it is typically adjudicated case by case.

Precedent introduces a further layer of constraint, since courts are generally expected to follow decisions of higher tribunals on materially identical questions. Yet the doctrine of stare decisis is not absolute; a court may depart from an earlier ruling where it is demonstrably unworkable or where its rationale has been eroded by subsequent developments. Such departures, however, carry a burden of justification that is rarely discharged lightly. The legitimacy of the judiciary, in this view, rests less on immutability than on the disciplined articulation of reasons.

questions.text: According to the passage, what do textualists contend judges must do?
options: Consider only the legislature's stated purpose
Confine themselves to the ordinary meaning of the enacted words
Follow the decisions of higher tribunals
Replace unclear statutes with their own rules

questions.text: According to the passage, when may a court depart from an earlier ruling?
options: Whenever the earlier ruling is inconvenient
Only when the legislature has amended the statute
Where the ruling is demonstrably unworkable or its rationale has been eroded
When the two parties agree to a different outcome

questions.text: What does the author imply about the justification required for departing from precedent?
options: It is a formality that courts can easily satisfy
It is a substantial burden that is rarely met lightly
It applies only to decisions made by lower courts
It is unnecessary once a ruling has stood for many years

questions.text: Which position is most consistent with the passage's view of judicial legitimacy?
options: Legitimacy depends on decisions never being revised
Legitimacy depends on judges avoiding all statutory interpretation
Legitimacy depends on the articulation of reasons for decisions
Legitimacy depends on the number of precedents cited

paragraph_translations: Hukuki akıl yürütme çoğunlukla bir kanunun lafzı ile onu canlandıran amaç arasındaki ayrım etrafında döner. Metinselciler, yargıçların yasama organının koyduğu sözcüklerin olağan anlamıyla sınırlı kalması gerektiğini savunur; aksi halde demokratik olarak hesap verebilir organlara ait bir işlevi gasp etmiş olurlar. Amaççılar ise buna karşılık, ifadeye katı bağlılığın kanunun hedeflediği amaçları boşa çıkarabileceğini ileri sürer. Ortaya çıkan gerilim soyut olarak nadiren çözülür ve genellikle olay olay hükme bağlanır.

Emsal kararlar ek bir kısıtlama katmanı oluşturur, çünkü mahkemelerden maddi olarak özdeş konularda üst mahkemelerin kararlarını izlemeleri genellikle beklenir. Yine de stare decisis ilkesi mutlak değildir; bir mahkeme, önceki bir kararın açıkça işlemez hale gelmesi ya da gerekçesinin sonraki gelişmelerle aşınmış olması durumunda bu karardan ayrılabilir. Ancak bu tür ayrılmaların gerekçelendirilme yükü ağırdır ve nadiren hafifçe karşılanır. Bu görüşe göre yargının meşruiyeti değişmezliğe değil, gerekçelerin disiplinli biçimde ifade edilmesine dayanır.
